Surely the most honourable of speech is the remembrance of Allah, and the head of wisdom is obedience to Him. The most truthful of sayings, the most eloquent of exhortations, and the most beautiful of narratives is the Book of Allah. The most trustworthy of bonds is faith in Allah, and the best of creeds is the creed of Ibrahim, and the best of traditions is the tradition of the prophets of Allah, and the best of guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family. The best of provisions is God-consciousness, the best of knowledge is that which benefits, the best of guidance is that which is followed, the best of richness is richness of the soul, and the best of what is cast into the heart is certainty. The adornment of speech is truthfulness, and the adornment of knowledge is doing good. The most noble of deaths is martyrdom, and the best of affairs is that with the best consequence. What is little and sufficient is better than what is much and distracting. The wretched is one who is wretched in the womb of his mother, and the fortunate is one who learns from others. The shrewdest of shrewdness is piety, and the most foolish of foolishness is immorality. The worst of narration is falsehood, the worst of affairs is their innovations, the worst of blindness is blindness of the heart, and the worst of regret is regret on the Day of Resurrection. The greatest of sinners in the sight of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a lying tongue. The worst of earnings is the earning of usury, the worst of consumption is consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly, and the most beautiful adornment for a man is tranquility with faith. Whoever seeks reputation, Allah will make him heard of. Whoever recognizes tribulation is patient with it, and whoever does not recognize it rejects it. Doubt is disbelief. Whoever is arrogant, Allah will abase him. Whoever obeys Satan disobeys Allah, and whoever disobeys Allah, Allah will punish him. Whoever thanks Allah, Allah will increase for him. Whoever is patient over calamity, Allah will aid him. Whoever relies on Allah, then Allah is sufficient for him. Do not anger Allah by pleasing any of His creation, and do not draw near to any of creation by distancing yourselves from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For indeed Allah has nothing between Him and any of creation that would grant him good or avert from him evil except through obedience to Him and seeking His pleasure. Indeed obedience to Allah is the attainment of every good that is sought, and salvation from every evil that is feared. Indeed Allah protects whoever obeys Him, and there is no protection from Him for whoever disobeys Him. The one fleeing from Allah will find no refuge, for indeed the command of Allah will descend to humiliate him even if the creatures dislike it. Everything that is coming is near. Muhammad, peace be upon him, said to me: This is a saying of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family.

key_terms.التَّقْوَى: God-consciousness (taqwa) -- the recurring theme of pious awareness that runs throughout the sermon as the supreme provision and virtue
key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury -- prohibited financial exploitation, listed as one of the worst forms of earning
key_terms.السَّكِينَة: tranquility/serenity -- described as the most beautiful adornment for a man when coupled with faith
key_terms.عَاقِبَة الْأُمُور: consequences of affairs -- referring to the ultimate outcomes of one's actions, both worldly and in the Hereafter
key_terms.مَال الْيَتِيم: wealth of the orphan -- consuming it unjustly is singled out as one of the gravest sins

ai.seo_question: What is the famous prophetic sermon about virtues and vices transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq in al-Amali al-Saduq?
ai.summary: This hadith records a famous prophetic sermon transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in response to Abu al-Sabah al-Kinani's inquiry about its attribution. The sermon is a comprehensive collection of wisdom aphorisms covering the foundations of faith, the hierarchy of virtues and vices, the consequences of human conduct, and the absolute sovereignty of Allah. The original audience understood these maxims as practical ethical guidance from the Prophet (PBUH), encompassing correct beliefs, moral conduct, social ethics, and ultimate accountability before Allah.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim from Safwan b. Yahya from Abi’l Sabah al-Kinani. He said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as): Inform me of this saying – whose saying is it? –: I ask Allah for faith and God-consciousness, and I seek refuge in Allah from the evil consequences of things. Surely, the most honourable of speech is the remembrance of Allah, and the peak of wisdom is obedience to Him. The most truthful of sayings, the most articulate of exhortations, and the most beautiful of stories is the Book of Allah. The most trustworthy virtue is faith in Allah, and the best of ways is the way of Ibrahim, and the best of traditions is the tradition of the prophets of Allah, and the best of guidance is the guidance of Muhammad (s), and the best of possessions is God-consciousness, and the best of knowledge is that which is of benefit, and the best of guidance is that which is followed, and the best of riches is being needless of the people, and the best thing to come to the heart is certainty. The adornment of speech is honesty, and the adornment of knowledge is beautification. The best of deaths is being killing in martyrdom. The best of affairs is that which has the best consequence and so on in goodness. The wretched is [known as] wretched in the womb of his mother, and the blissful is he who learns from the example of others. The best goodness is the pious, and the most foolish of fools is the immoral. The evillest of reports is the lie, and the evillest of affairs is innovation [in religion], and the evillest of blindness is the blindness of the heart, and the worst of regrets is the regret on the Day of Resurrection. The greatest of sinners with Allah is one with a lying tongue. The evillest of gains is gaining usury, and the evillest of consumption is wrongfully consuming the wealth of the orphan. The most beautiful adornment for a man is serenity in faith.

Whoever desires reputation, Allah will ruin his reputation. Whoever recognizes [the nature of] tribulation is patient with it, and whoever does not recognize it denies it. Doubt is disbelief. Whoever is arrogant, Allah will put him down. Whoever follows Satan disobeys Allah, and whoever disobeys Allah, Allah will punish him. Whoever thanks Allah, Allah increases for him. Whoever is patient over a calamity, Allah helps him. Whoever relies on Allah, Allah will be sufficient or him.

Do not disobey Allah to please one of His creatures, and do not gain the proximity of a creature by distancing yourself from Allah, for there is nothing obliging Allah to give goodness to or repel harm from the creation except obedience and seeking His pleasure. Surely, obeying Allah is the triumph of every desired good, and the triumph over every fearful evil. Surely, Allah protects he who obeys Him, and He does not protect he who disobeys Him. One who retreats from Allah will find no place to retreat to, for surely, the command of Allah will come down to humiliate him, even if the creatures may be averse. Everything that is coming is near – whatever Allah willed has occurred, and whatever He has not willed will not occur. Help one another in righteousness and piety, and do not help one another in sin and aggression. Fear Allah, for Allah is stern in reprisal.
He said: So, Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) said to me: This is a saying of the Messenger of Allah (s).
